subroutine ranges_init(s)
      use xmpi_module
      implicit none
      type(spacepars)    :: s

      imin_ee = 2
      imax_ee = s%nx
      if (s%ny>0) then
         jmin_ee = 2
         jmax_ee = s%ny
      else
         jmin_ee = 1
         jmax_ee = 1
      endif

      imin_uu = 2
      imax_uu = s%nx-1
      if (s%ny>0) then
         jmin_uu = 2
         jmax_uu = s%ny
      else
         jmin_uu = 1
         jmax_uu = 1
      endif

      imin_vv = 2
      imax_vv = s%nx
      if (s%ny>0) then
         jmin_vv = 2
         jmax_vv = s%ny-1
      else
         jmin_vv = 1
         jmax_vv = 1
      endif

      imin_zs = 2
      imax_zs = s%nx
      if (s%ny>0) then
         jmin_zs = 2
         jmax_zs = s%ny
      else
         jmin_zs = 1
         jmax_zs = 1
      endif

call space_distribute_space (sglobal,s,par)
#endif

      call ranges_init(s)

      ! nonh_init does not always need to be called
      if (par%wavemodel==WAVEMODEL_NONH) call nonh_init(s,par)

original_claims.base: [L53-L62] (MED/distributed-state-consistency) MPI_MIN is applied independently to idrift and jdrift, so if different overlapping ranks produce the minima the reduced coordinate pair need not come from any single rank's drifter update.
original_claims.audit: [L41-L62] (HIGH/MPI-ownership/reduction) Every rank whose local index test succeeds advances the drifter, while idrift and jdrift are reduced independently with MPI_MIN, so overlapping ownership or differing local updates can select coordinates from different ranks and create a position no rank computed.

prior_unverified_refutation.rationale: Overlapping ranks use the same global drifter indices and distributed grid metrics, and flow synchronizes both velocity components before drifter is called. The predictor and second-order branches repeat those exchanges, and the final nonhydrostatic correction exchanges them internally, so overlapping updates are identical and independent minima cannot splice differing positions on this path.

items.call_path: libxbeach_module:executestep -> flow (velocity halo exchanges on every active branch) -> drifter; each rank either updates both coordinates under one joint bounds test or replaces both with the same sentinel
items.reason: Independent reductions could splice coordinates only if qualifying ranks supplied different coordinate pairs. The active call path synchronizes uu and vv before drifter and uses the same distributed metrics for the same global locations; the joint bounds test prevents a rank from supplying only one coordinate. The source does not demonstrate differing overlapping updates.
items.canonical_ready_ko: MPI drifter는 `flow` 직후 호출되며, 활성 유동 분기마다 `uu`와 `vv` halo를 교환한다 (`models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/flow_timestep.F90:630`, `models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/libxbeach.F90:301`). 각 rank는 하나의 결합 경계검사로 두 좌표를 함께 갱신하거나 두 좌표를 모두 sentinel로 바꾼 뒤 각각 `MPI_MIN`을 적용한다 (`models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/drifters.F90:40`). 따라서 제공된 경로에서는 서로 다른 rank의 좌표 성분이 섞인다는 결함이 입증되지 않는다.

original_claims.audit: [L103-L112] (MED/input error handling) Species-name reads record iostat in ier but never inspect it, so a short or malformed species list can leave names undefined and fail later in a misleading way.

evidence.quote:
integer function count_lines(f)
      !
      ! returns number of lines in file f
      ! to be called by all, xmaster will count
      ! result is broadcasted to all
      !
      use xmpi_module
      use filefunctions
      character(len=*), intent(in) :: f
      integer lines,fid,ierr
      if(xmaster) then
         fid = create_new_fid()
         open(fid,file=f)
         lines = 0
         ierr = 0
         do while(ierr == 0)
            read(fid,*,iostat=ierr)
            if (ierr == 0) lines = lines+1
         enddo
         close(fid)
      endif
#ifdef USEMPI
      call xmpi_bcast(lines,readkey_inio)
#endif
      count_lines = lines

! 1) Read veggiefile with veggie species
         par%nveg = count_lines(par%veggiefile)

         if (xmaster) then
            allocate(veg(par%nveg))
            fid=create_new_fid()
            call check_file_exist(par%veggiefile)
            open(fid,file=par%veggiefile)
            do i=1,par%nveg
               read(fid,'(a)',iostat=ier) veg(i)%name
            enddo
            close(fid)

! 3)  Allocate and read vegetation properties for every species
            do is=1,par%nveg  ! for each species
               ! read vegetation file name
               call check_file_exist(veg(is)%name)
               ! Check if it is canopy flow model type
               veg(is)%isCanopy = readkey_int(veg(is)%name,'isCanopy',0,0,1,bcast=.false.,strict=.true.)

items.call_path: veggie_init -> count_lines(first open/read pass) -> second open and fixed-count '(a)' reads -> check_file_exist for each resulting name
items.reason: For an unchanged ordinary text file, the first pass determines the exact number of records and '(a)' accepts nonnumeric text, so the claimed static short/malformed-list undefined-name path does not stand. The second pass nevertheless records and ignores iostat; an intervening file change or read failure is reported only later, potentially against a stale or undefined name.

original_claims.audit: [L209-L211,L319-L323] (MED/unchecked dimension contract) The implementation requires n>=2 (division by n-1 and references to sigz(2) and sigz(n-1)) but neither checks nor documents that precondition in the interface.

module vsm_u_xb_module
   implicit none
   save
   private
   public vsm_u_XB
contains
   subroutine vsm_u_XB (  ue    ,ve    ,h     ,ks    ,               &
   rho   ,tauwx ,tauwy ,theta ,               &
   urms  ,omega ,k     ,diss  ,               &
   e ,er ,fcvisc,facdel,ws    ,               &
   fw    ,facdf ,swglm ,n     ,sigz  ,        &
   uz    ,vz    ,ustz  ,nutz  ,               &
   ue_sed,ve_sed )

integer, intent(in)   :: n                 ! number of vertical layers
      real*8,  intent(out)  :: sigz(n)           ! vertical sigma grid (0 at bottom, 1 at surface)

!   generate vertical grid

      hd=1.d0
      do i=1,n
         sigz(i)=0.01d0*(hd/0.01d0)**(float(i-1)/float(n-1))/hd
      enddo

dsig(1)=0.5d0*sigz(2)
      do i=2,n-1
         dsig(i)=(sigz(i+1)-sigz(i-1))*0.5d0
      enddo
      dsig(n)=0.5d0*(sigz(n)-sigz(n-1))

! XBeach uses same input for Van Rijn, 1993 (quasi 3d), but doesn't use this module

                  tauwy=s%windnv(i,j)*tauw

                  par%rho      ,tauwx ,tauwy ,s%thetamean(i,j)-s%alfaz(i,j),  &
                  s%urms(i,j)  ,s%sigm(i,j)  ,s%k(i,j)       ,s%Dr(i,j)  ,    &

items.reason: The XBeach solver call path excludes n<2, so this is not a default solver failure. The routine is nevertheless public and its local interface neither states nor checks n>=2, while its arithmetic requires it. The original interface-contract warning stands at reduced scope and severity.
items.canonical_ready_ko: XBeach 내부 호출은 `par%nz>1`일 때만 `par%nz`를 `n`으로 전달하므로 기본 solver 경로에서 `n=1`은 도달하지 않는다 (`models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/flow_timestep.F90:956`). 그러나 `vsm_u_XB`는 공개 모듈 절차이고, 인터페이스에는 `n>=2` 조건이나 실행 검사가 없는데 구현은 `n-1`로 나누고 `sigz(2)`·`sigz(n-1)`을 참조한다 (`models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/vsm_u_XB.f90:5`, `models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/vsm_u_XB.f90:38`, `models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/vsm_u_XB.f90:209`, `models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/vsm_u_XB.f90:319`). 외부 직접 호출 시 `n>=2`가 필요한 인터페이스 계약 경고로 유지한다.

original_claims.audit: [L68,L78,L148,L158] (MED/feature-configuration) Combined MPI_netcdf configurations omit the feature preprocessor definitions provided by the separate MPI and netCDF configurations, leaving wrapper feature selection inconsistent with the configuration name.

prior_unverified_refutation.rationale: The dynamic DLL sources have no MPI/netCDF preprocessing selection at all: libxbeach_dynamic.F90 delegates to libxbeach_module and introspection.F90 accesses that library through module interfaces. Both features are selected while compiling the dependent static library, so the wrapper definitions are redundant and their omission is not a feature mismatch.

original_claims.base: [L139-L162] (MED/Fortran-semantics) The proposed replacement for saved scratch arrays omits a deallocation example and assumes automatic removal at subroutine exit, while the original saved allocation can retain dimensions across calls; callers with changing local-grid sizes therefore lack a safe lifecycle contract.
original_claims.audit: [L139-L154] (MED/documented-allocation-limitation) The documented saved scratch-array pattern allocates only once and explicitly leaves wrong-sized arrays possible when subsequent spacepar instances have different dimensions.

prior_unverified_refutation.rationale: The finding treats a deliberately criticized example as the recommended lifecycle: lines 152-154 explicitly warn that SAVE can retain the wrong dimensions, and lines 156-162 replace it with a local allocatable without SAVE. Such a local allocatable is automatically deallocated on procedure exit, so the replacement allocates the current dimensions on each call and needs no explicit deallocation example; the cited passage does not establish a defect in that guidance.
prior_unverified_refutation.neutralizer_quote:
This solution, however, is not good when one should define more than
one spacepar variable (apart from sglobal and slocal). Then the size
of the 'saved' matrices could be wrong.

I suggest to simply allocate these scratch arrays:

  real*8, dimension(:,:), allocatable :: xyz
  allocate(xyz(s%nx+1,s%ny+1))

According to the fortran95 standard, these allocated arrays are 
automatically removed at the exit of the subroutine.
prior_unverified_refutation.assessment: The neutralizer is exact and dispositive once the immediately preceding criticized SAVE example is included.

evidence.quote:
In a number of subroutines, some scratch arrays are declared save, 
as in:

  real*8, dimension(:,:), allocatable, save :: xyz
  if ( .not. allocated(xyz)) allocate(xyz(nx+1,ny+1))

In almost all cases, an automatic declaration would suffice, like

  real*8, dimension(s%nx+1,s%ny+1) :: xyz

However, I understand that some compilers/linkers have difficulties
with large program stacks, so that explains the 'save' solution.

This solution, however, is not good when one should define more than
one spacepar variable (apart from sglobal and slocal). Then the size
of the 'saved' matrices could be wrong.

I suggest to simply allocate these scratch arrays:

  real*8, dimension(:,:), allocatable :: xyz
  allocate(xyz(s%nx+1,s%ny+1))

According to the fortran95 standard, these allocated arrays are 
automatically removed at the exit of the subroutine.

items.call_path: documentation example only: saved allocatable anti-pattern -> explicit warning -> local unsaved allocatable replacement
items.reason: The finding reverses the document's recommendation. The retained-dimension SAVE pattern is presented and then explicitly rejected; the proposed local allocatable has no SAVE and is intended to be allocated for the current s dimensions on each invocation. The absence of an explicit deallocate example is not the claimed lifecycle defect.
items.canonical_ready_ko: `README.parallel`은 SAVE allocatable 패턴을 권장하는 것이 아니라, 여러 `spacepar` 크기를 사용할 때 저장 배열의 크기가 틀릴 수 있다고 명시적으로 경고한 뒤 SAVE가 없는 지역 allocatable을 대안으로 제시한다 (`models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/doc/README.parallel:139`). 따라서 이 문단을 saved workspace lifecycle 결함으로 분류한 주장은 문맥을 반대로 읽은 것으로 기각한다.

base: [L117-L118,L157-L158,L189-L190,L201-L202,L233-L234,L245-L246,L287-L288,L327-L328] (MED/uninitialized-copy) Getters copy temporary outputs regardless of read status and copy full temporary arrays even when the attribute is shorter, propagating undefined values on errors or unwritten elements.
[L49-L53] (MED/inquiry-error-handling) Attribute inquiry overwrites the attnum lookup status and copies local type and length outputs even when their inquiry fails.
audit: [L49-L51] (LOW/error-propagation) The attribute-ID lookup status is unconditionally overwritten by the subsequent attribute inquiry, obscuring any distinct failure of the requested attnum lookup.

[L52-L53,L117-L118,L157-L158,L189-L190,L201-L202,L233-L234,L245-L246,L287-L288,L327-L328] (MED/undefined-value) Inquiry and getter wrappers copy uninitialized local outputs after failed calls, and integer array getters also copy undefined tail elements when the destination exceeds the attribute length.

prior_unverified_refutation.rationale: attnum is an output here, not an independently requested attribute-number input: both calls query exactly the same ncid, varid and name. The F77 inquiry-family contract gives these two name-based inquiries the same invalid-ID/missing-attribute failure conditions, so the second inquiry preserves those failures rather than hiding a demonstrated distinct attnum lookup error; the supplied other_wording concerns a different issue.
prior_unverified_refutation.neutralizer_quote:
function nf90_inquire_attribute(ncid, varid, name, xtype, len, attnum)
    integer,             intent( in)           :: ncid, varid
    character (len = *), intent( in)           :: name
    integer,             intent(out), optional :: xtype, len, attnum
    integer                                    :: nf90_inquire_attribute

    integer                          :: local_xtype, local_len

    ! Do we need to worry about not saving the state from this call?
    if(present(attnum)) &
      nf90_inquire_attribute = nf_inq_attid(ncid, varid, name, attnum)
    nf90_inquire_attribute   = nf_inq_att  (ncid, varid, name, local_xtype, local_len)
prior_unverified_refutation.assessment: It addresses only audit B2. It does not neutralize base A4/A5 or audit B3, and lines 52-53 plus every scalar/converting getter directly confirm unconditional copies after the status-returning call.

external_primary_sources.title: NetCDF-Fortran: The NetCDF Fortran 77 Interface Guide, section 7.3 NF_INQ_ATT Family
external_primary_sources.use: NF_INQ_ATT and NF_INQ_ATTID share the documented invalid ncid, invalid varid, and missing-attribute failure conditions. This supports refuting only the alleged distinct attnum lookup failure in a stable dataset.

external_primary_sources.title: NetCDF-Fortran: 7 Attributes, section 7.4 NF90_GET_ATT
external_primary_sources.quote: All elements of the vector of attribute values are returned, so you must provide enough space to hold them.
external_primary_sources.use: The external library returns the attribute's elements; it does not define extra caller elements. The wrapper must not copy uninitialized temporary tails as if they were outputs.

items.call_path: bundled nf90 wrapper -> status-returning F77 nf_inq_att/nf_get_att_* -> unconditional assignment of local temporaries to optional/scalar/full-array outputs

subdispositions.reason: In a stable dataset, both name-based inquiry calls have the same documented lookup failure conditions, so overwriting the first status does not hide a demonstrated distinct attnum lookup error.

The wrapper copies local_xtype/local_len and getter temporaries regardless of returned status. Converting integer array wrappers additionally copy size(values) elements although the external API defines only the attribute elements, leaving any excess temporary tail undefined.

items.canonical_ready_ko: 번들된 legacy netCDF-Fortran 래퍼의 `nf90_inquire_attribute`는 같은 이름을 조회하는 `nf_inq_attid`와 `nf_inq_att`의 상태 중 뒤의 상태를 반환한다. 안정된 dataset에서는 두 호출의 공식 실패 조건이 같으므로 별도의 `attnum` 오류가 가려진다는 주장은 기각한다 (Unidata netCDF-Fortran F77 Interface Guide §7.3, acc. 2026-09-09; `models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/lib/win32/netcdff90/netcdf_attributes.f90:40`). 그러나 래퍼는 실패 상태에서도 미초기화된 type·length 및 scalar 임시값을 출력에 복사하고, 정수 변환 배열은 실제 속성 길이보다 큰 임시 배열 전체를 복사한다 (`models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/lib/win32/netcdff90/netcdf_attributes.f90:52`, `models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/lib/win32/netcdff90/netcdf_attributes.f90:187`, `models/XBeach/raw/source_code/trunk/lib/win32/netcdff90/netcdf_attributes.f90:231`). 이는 XBeach solver 결함이 아니라 포함된 외부 netCDF 래퍼의 오류·출력 계약 위험이다.
